assumptions.claim: cfg_valid is asserted only when op_i and key_len_i represent a legal configuration, and does not glitch while the control module samples it.
assumptions.cond: when configuration is being loaded (during in_valid_i and in_ready_o handshake or later usage)
assumptions.risk: Illegal or glitched configuration could cause incorrect cipher mode selection, invalid key length, or unpredictable state transitions, potentially bypassing security restrictions.

assumptions.risk: False or glitching error assertions may trigger premature or unnecessary key_clear_o/data_out_clear_o cycles, destroying secret material or causing denial of service.

security_implications: This instance is the control hub of the AES cipher core, connecting key clear, data out clear, masking PRNG updates, and alert escalation. The control module internally decides when to zeroize secret key and output data, and it propagates fatal/system errors to the top-level alert. Any flaw in the control logic—such as a missed error, glitched clear signal, or deadlocked handshake—could directly cause secrets to remain in registers after a fault, or allow leakage through side channels. The assumptions on external inputs are critical for the security guarantees of the entire AES module.
